quest.title: Thesis Proposal: He Shall not Pass
quest.description: Strange rumors are spreading in Port Ormos about a "groaning Akademiya researcher." You wonder what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: Ugh... My academic career has been sunk before it could even start...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: A scholar? Why bother being a scholar? If I had learned to draw in the Akademiya and became an illustrator, I wouldn't have ended up here... Haha... Hahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, when we first heard that there was an Akademiya researcher in Port Ormos who groans all day... Paimon thought it was some kind of strange tale.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But hey, guess he's real. Hey, "groaning Akademiya researcher"!

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: What...? "Groaning Akademiya researcher"? Are you talking about me?

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: *sigh* If you'd met me in the past, I would debate the veracity of such a slanderous title. But now... forget it.

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: Go back to where you came from, little one. Don't disturb a young man, mired, adrift, without a future. People like me should just shrivel like a silent mushroom in the dark corner of the forest...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: At least the Akademiya's resources wouldn't be wasted then. I might even be taken back there as some special mushroom sample to be dissected by some real scholar...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: "Jami the Mushroom Sample." Wouldn't it be funny if that's how I wound up being remembered by history...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jami? Oh, so that's your name.

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: Yeah. What about it, little one?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The name's Paimon! Not "little one"!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #And I'm {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon. Right, noted. So, how may I help you...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we just heard about the rumors of "groaning Akademiya researcher" in Port Ormos and wanted to know what was going on.

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: *sigh*... What's going on, you say? Well, have you heard of this thing that happens for us researchers called "publishing our research"?

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: Publishing independent research is how we prove that we are capable, self-sufficient scholars. That's how we graduate from under our mentor's tutelage and enter the academic world, where we can then gain renown...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: That way, we can travel to places in Teyvat in the name of collecting research material, with research grants sufficient to cover even fine food and drink!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fine food and drink, huh... Say, you wouldn't mind elaborating on that, would you?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Uh, I was just saying... In truth, I dream of doing great things in the academic world.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Good food, traveling, fame, things like these are just side benefits. I wouldn't reject them, of course, but... *cough* Either way, we're getting off topic.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Anyway, I'm stuck at the "publish your research" part. The courses at Akademiya have a tight schedule already, and I have to get my thesis proposal passed in time.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: My proposals have been rejected twice. "The Edibleness of Mushrooms on the Back of Shroomboars" was the first one. I actually thought that one was pretty good...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it certainly sounds like a good subject. One that warrants a couple hundred experiments, for sure!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: I know, right? But my mentor just said "is this even worth looking into?" and refused my request... Absolutely ridiculous.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: The second time, I applied to research "The Ecological Environment and Aquaculture of Floating Hydro Fungi," but got rejected again by my mentor, who called the topic too unambitious...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: The deadline for submitting the thesis proposal was drawing near, and so I wrote up a very ambitious proposal in a fit of pique... You know, as a way of saying "you old man, how dare you call me unambitious!"

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: I didn't think that my mentor would let it pass or that it would get praise in the Akademiya. But there was no way back from there, so my report became...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Became what?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Heh... a "Study on the Defense Deficiencies of Biological Structures in Response to Hostile Stressors"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, Paimon doesn't know what you're talking about. Doesn't sound delicious or interesting either.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: The research topic of your study should ideally be a bit obscure. To put it in simple terms, creatures in combat will more or less reveal some weaknesses in their defenses.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Some weak spots, which should have been well protected, will end up exposed when they make certain movements. And those are the Weaknesses I'm collecting for my research.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's still kinda hard to understand... but it sounds awesome!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Well, being awesome doesn't help you fight monsters or take pictures of research materials. I'm just a fragile researcher. This subject is way too dangerous for me!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: How am I supposed to finish this whole thing...? And with an unfinished thesis, I won't be able to graduate...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Fighting monsters... Hah, whatever. Let's just do it. I might get heavily injured, but maybe my mentor might take pity on me and grant a pass to this poor student...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Please don't do that!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: But my thesis proposal has already been submitted. There's no time to switch topics. What can I do?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: I was too impulsive for my own good. Some researcher I am! I should just go feed myself to a Rishboland Tiger! Wait, no. That might hurt. Maybe I should drown myself in the river near Vimara Village instead. The water's cool and clean there...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, poor guy! It's partially his fault for ending up like this, but still...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's just help him, shall we?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, now that you've said this much...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: R—Really? But it's a very dangerous job...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No worries! We're pretty good at fighting monsters!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Ah, thank you! Thank you! Does this mean I can finish my thesis now? I'd even sell myself to you if you can help me do that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, you totally don't have to! And we don't wanna buy you, anyway...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Sorry... apologies for my lack of composure. How about this, then? Let's go to the testing ground I've prepared.

choices.text: Looks like he has some ulterior motives...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't realize that we had walked all this way here...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: There's no other way around, I fear.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is too far from Port Ormos...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: Well, this is about my test subjects after all. You know, my mentor wanted me to observe every living being in Teyvat. An impossible task, I tell you!

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: And that's why I started by researching creatures from Sumeru and Liyue...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: By the way, please hold this. It's a special potion for my research that works within the testing grounds.

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: It's called the "Fayz Potion," and it was formulated by my seniors at Amurta. It's expensive and complicated to make, so I've only managed to make a few...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's this potion gotta do with your experiment?

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: Here's how it works: you will subjectively feel that time will slow down in a very extreme manner after taking the "Fayz Potion." It'll feel like one moment is eternal.

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: This way, you can do more detailed photography and observations!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a moment, couldn't you just do that yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: I thought so too, but it's not that simple.

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: As I said, you will subjectively feel time slowing down... But your body may not be able to keep up if you aren't agile enough...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: For example, if you quaff a Fayz Potion as a Spinocrocodile pounces on you but you aren't agile enough to dodge its lunging attack...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: Then you will see how its claws are ever so close to your face, yet your body just won't move out of the way...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: "Why can't I move my body!?" You may think to yourself. But it will be of no use. The paws will still stay so close to you that you can even see the dirty water and mud-stains on it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: So, don't underestimate your opponents just because you feel that time is moving slowly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will do!

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: The fate of my research is in your hands...
